title: Tenant burst safety net and deferred scaling playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Postmortem follow-up for the 2026-03 hosted API GPU capacity exhaustion event. Users experienced long tail latency and queue buildup when several high-throughput tenants simultaneously ramped. This ticket defines a safety-net architecture that combines conservative admission for speculative bursts, a deferred scaling window (short-term soft capacity), and tenant-aware admission scoring to prevent cascade queue amplification. The goal is to reduce outage surface area during sudden tenant spikes while preserving stable latency for steady traffic.
acceptance_criteria: New admission score computed per request including tenant burst score and recent KV cache hit rate
Deferred scaling window implemented: requests within 30s burst window get prioritized but limited to N% of pool capacity
No SLO regressions for steady-state tenants in staged rollout (latency P95 unchanged within 5%)
Dashboard tile showing tenant burst credits, deferred-scale usage, and queue depth per pool
Automated fallback: when deferred pool usage exceeds threshold, system soft-declines low-priority requests with 429 and informative retry-after
implementation_plan: Week 1: Instrumentation - add tenant burst counters, per-tenant short-term qps window, and KV cache hit telemetry (PR: github.com/redwood/serving/pull/1287)
Week 1: Telemetry dashboard - Grafana panel for burst credit burn and pool deferred capacity
Week 2: Admission scoring - implement tenant burst score and weighted admission decision (feature branch: feature/burst-score)
Week 2: Deferred scaling controller - implement 30s window soft-capacity and rate limiter for deferred allocations
Week 3: Canary rollout - start with 2% of traffic in a single region and monitor P50/P95/P99 latency and queue depth
Week 4: Gradual ramp to 25% traffic using canary manager; collect feedback and iterate on thresholds
